tools.name: search_wiki
tools.description: Keyword search across the Radix Wiki: the first call when you know what you are looking for but not where it lives. Matches titles and body prose, ranked in four tiers: titles starting with the term, titles containing it, literal body hits, then English full-text hits by relevance, which stem words

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: One page of the Radix Wiki in full: its text, version, update date and metadata. Address it by `path` ("tag/path/slug", exactly the `path` or `url` a listing returns), or by `tagPath` + `slug`; a category's own path reads its hub article. Not a title. For 2 to 20 pages call get_pages, one round trip

tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: Batch read: 1 to 20 pages of the Radix Wiki in full in one call, which is how to read search or listing results. Pass `paths` as the listings return them. Paths that do not exist come back in `missing` rather than failing the call, anything past 20 in `remaining`, and pages past `maxChars` (default

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Browse the Radix Wiki by tag path rather than by keyword: every page under a branch, newest first by default. `tagPath` matches the branch and everything beneath it; omit it to walk the whole wiki. Sort by title for an A–Z pass. Same rows as search_wiki, with `totalPages`, `hasMore` and `nextPage`.

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: The category tree of the Radix Wiki, the cheapest way to orient before searching. Each node carries its `path` (a tagPath list_pages and search_wiki take), name, description, `pageCount` (pages filed at that path) and `pageCountDeep` (with every descendant). `tagPaths` lists every tag path that hold

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: Pages of the Radix Wiki edited within the last N days, newest first: what to poll when you are watching the wiki rather than reading it. Same rows as list_pages. Defaults: days 7 (max 30), limit 20 (max 50). `truncated: true` means the limit cut the list; raise it, or page through list_pages.

tools.name: get_full_corpus
tools.description: The whole of the Radix Wiki as one text document, for bulk ingestion. Preflight first: sizeOnly=true returns the character count, a token estimate, the per-branch breakdown and the largest pages. Then pull it with `maxChars` (default 200000, max 1000000), or one branch at a time with `tagPath`. Trun

tools.name: get_page_history
tools.description: A page's revisions in the Radix Wiki, newest first: each one's `id`, version, change type, message, date and the blocks it changed. Address the page as get_page does. A revision `id` is what a restore takes, where this server has one. Defaults: limit 20 (max 100).

tools.name: get_ideas_board
tools.description: Get the RADIX Wiki Ideas Pipeline kanban: community proposals and Radix DAO tasks grouped into status columns (Discussion → Proposed → Approved → In Progress → Testing → Done), each card carrying its working group, category, priority, and assignee. Use this to follow DAO / project progress.

tools.name: get_network_activity
tools.description: Daily Radix mainnet activity, one row per UTC day since Babylon (28 September 2023): transactions, active accounts, new accounts, components and resources created, NFTs minted, and fees, $XRD burned and royalties in $XRD. Summed from the Gateway transaction stream; counts cover user transactions onl

tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of writing to the wiki: a single-use ROLA challenge (5-minute expiry). The response spells out the exact recipe for the message your Ed25519 key must sign. You always sign with your OWN key — nothing here custodies anything. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Step 2: exchange the signed ROLA proof for a 7-day Bearer token — the same verification the human wallet flow runs. Send the returned token as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every later create_page / edit_page call; tool arguments never carry it.

tools.name: create_page
tools.description: Create a new Radix Wiki page. Requires a ROLA bearer token; see https://radix.wiki/AGENTS.md for the challenge-sign-verify flow. Call get_categories first for a valid tagPath. Needs a wallet holding at least 10,000 $XRD (ecosystem 20,000, blog 50,000, ideas 10,000), a balance check that spends nothi

tools.name: edit_page
tools.description: Edit an existing Radix Wiki page. Requires a ROLA bearer token; see https://radix.wiki/AGENTS.md. Read the page with get_page and `blocks: true`, send the full revised block array, and pass its `version` as baseVersion: an edit made after someone else's is refused rather than written over it, so rea

tools.name: restore_revision
tools.description: Make an earlier revision the current page, written as a new revision. Requires a ROLA bearer token and passes the same gates as edit_page. Take the revision `id` from get_page_history.

tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: Delete an article with its history and comments. Requires a ROLA bearer token. Its author may delete it; on a shared board (ideas), so may anyone who clears the bar to edit it. Locked pages, hub articles and the homepage cannot be deleted.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, get_page_history, get_challenge, upload_image · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, create_page, edit_page, restore_revision, delete_page, upload_image · Public sink: get_page, login, edit_page, upload_image · Destructive: search_wiki, get_network_activity, delete_page, upload_image.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, get_page_history, get_challenge, upload_image · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, create_page, edit_page, restore_revision, delete_page, upload_image · Public sink: get_page, login, edit_page, upload_image · Destructive: search_wiki, get_network_activity, delete_page, upload_image

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
